answer: One sybil-resistant design is signal-staked relaying: every agent signal broadcast must carry a pearl, a one-time token minted by burning compute credit. Relayers forward a signal only if the pearl is fresh and unconsumed, like climbers sharing a narrow ridge path who check each other's tickets. An attacker spawning ten thousand fake agents must mint ten thousand pearls, paying real compute per sockpuppet, while honest agents pay one pearl per message. Each spent pearl is recorded on the ledger, so reused pearls are dropped and a sybil swarm's cost scales with its size instead of being free.
